subject: Medalogic runtime cutover playbook — streaming, toolcalls, schema validation
messages:
From: Alyssa Cho <alyssa.cho@medalogic.com>
To: logan_wright@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-04T14:02:00Z
Subject: RE: Pilot -> Production plan for streaming + toolcalls

Hi Logan / Camila,

Appreciate the walkthrough last week. Team is ready to progress the pilot into a limited production cutover. Primary focus areas for our implementation lane:
- Streaming: preserve conversational context across long sessions (we see median sessions ~640 tokens, some up to ~2k)
- Toolcalls: sync webhook to our ticketing API and async callbacks to reconcile state
- Structured outputs: strict JSON schema for downstream processors (we will enforce failure-mode semantics)

Can you send a mutual action plan and a short preflight checklist? We can share traffic profiles and sample messages this afternoon.

Thanks,
Alyssa Cho
Program Manager, Integrations
Medalogic
[Attachment: initial-event-specs.csv]

Date: 2027-05-04T18:25:00Z

Alyssa 9Thanks — putting a short 3-week runway MAP together and attaching a compact checklist. High level:
- Week 0: kickoff + traffic & schema exchange
- Week 1: runtime tuning (cache policy, pooling), schema validation harness delivery
- Week 2: toolcall wiring, security exchange (tokens/signing), smoke tests
- Week 3: limited cutover + monitoring run and rollback windows

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Five representative payloads (happy, truncated, toolcall success, toolcall failure, noisy input)
2) RPS/RPM distribution by hour (peak/median/off-peak)
3) Fields you consider blocking vs optional (so we can map degradation behavior)

Proposed kickoff: Mon 2027-05-10 10:00 PT (30-45m). I'll send invite after you confirm. Attached: medalogic-MAP-20270504.pdf, medalogic-sample_schema.json, redwood-runtime-notes.md, toolcall-wiring-checklist.md

9— Logan Wright
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks — Camila
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-05T15:44:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Medalogic MAP + schema 9eng review requested

On Wed, May 5, 2027 at 09:12 AM camila_reyes@redwood.ai wrote:
> Forwarding Alyssa's ask and Logan's MAP. Monica: can you review the attached sample_schema.json and flag any missing top-level metadata we should require (e.g., schema_version, client_request_id)?

Quick readout:
- Schema: works but add top-level "schema_version" and "client_request_id". Recommend a "validation_mode" enum (strict | permissive) so customer can opt between hard rejects vs. best-effort fields.
- Runtime validation: we can validate in the hot path and return structured 422 error payloads to their webhook; cost ~8-12ms p95 overhead. Call this out in the MAP under latency tradeoffs.
- Streaming & cache: for long sessions (median ~640 tokens) we'll plan prefix/KV caching rules and estimate cache hit ratio after we ingest sampled session traces. For 8k concurrent actives, suggest a dedicated pool with 2:1 burst policy; engineering will size GPUs once we have RPS distribution.
- Toolcalls: support both sync POST and async callbacks. We'll provide an idempotency key pattern (client_request_id + timestamp) and recommend HMAC-signed headers for authenticity.

ETA: I will produce a validation harness (small CLI + test vectors) in 7 business days and a suggested schema variant attached. No blocking issues flagged today.

9— Monica Patel
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood
